messages:
Priya Patel: heads up — new customer Polaris Labs completed signup but their app gets 403 using the API key they see in the console. console shows a key present but it's attached to project 'internal-tools-staging' not Polaris
Alex Chen: can you paste the org/tenant id and the key id from the console?
Priya Patel: org: org_01G8XK4P, console key id: key_02AB9C; app error is immediate: curl returns 403. here's the repro we ran:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer key_02AB9C" \ \ 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-neo-8b","input":"hello"}' | jq
```

Response:
```
{"error":"forbidden","reason":"project_mismatch","expected_project":"polaris-prod","actual_project":"internal-tools-staging"}
```

Sam Ortiz: ack. that payload makes it obvious — key exists but scoped wrong. any chance the provisioning webhook mapped to the wrong project?
Priya Patel: customer says they hit the invite flow and selected their org. no manual step. billing shows a trial assigned to polaris-prod though.
Ingrid M: pinging infra — @DeployBot can you surface the provisioning webhook payload for org_01G8XK4P and the lambda run that created key_02AB9C?
DeployBot: [automated] provisioning_event: ts=1767119868, org=org_01G8XK4P, email=ops@polaris.example, env=staging, template=internal-tools-template, created_key=key_02AB9C, created_project=internal-tools-staging
Alex Chen: aha — payload contains env=staging which caused the template router to pick internal-tools-template. that shouldn't happen for self-serve signups. looks like the router matched on env prior to tenant binding.
Sam Ortiz: mitigation options: 1) rebind the key to polaris-prod now (manual admin attach). 2) create a new key in the correct project and rotate for the customer. which do we want?
Priya Patel: customer prefers quick fix — rebind is fine as long as it's atomic and we rotate soon. please include repro steps so we can explain cause.
Ingrid M: I can run the rebind. command (internal admin CLI):

```bash
# run as infra-admin
redwood-admin keys rebind --key-id key_02AB9C --from-project internal-tools-staging --to-project polaris-prod --actor infra-service
```

Ingrid M: I'll run it in 10m and watch logs.
Alex Chen: after rebind we should check token scopes and policies to ensure no extra perms were granted when moved. also update audit log entry.
Sam Ortiz: root cause: provisioning router uses payload matching order; the legacy webhook included env param in vendor SSO which caused a false positive to internal templates. fix: change router to require explicit project mapping when org claim present, and deprioritize env-based rules.
Priya Patel: please add a short note I can send to the customer explaining what went wrong and what we changed.
Ingrid M: rebind complete. logs:

```
[1767119932] rebind.start key=key_02AB9C from=internal-tools-staging to=polaris-prod actor=infra-service
[1767119934] iam.check scopes_ok
[1767119940] rebind.complete key=key_02AB9C new_project=polaris-prod
```

Ingrid M: verified customer app now returns 200 for same curl above.
Priya Patel: sending update to Polaris: "We found an automated provisioning rule matched your signup payload (it included an env=staging flag) which routed the created API key to an internal staging project. We've re-assigned that key to your project (polaris-prod) and rotated the key on request. We're also patching the provisioning router to ignore env flags for self-serve signups to prevent recurrence."
Alex Chen: filed infra ticket INF-4893 to adjust router priority and add a unit test for webhook payload permutations.
Sam Ortiz: recommend we also add a detection alert if created_project != claimed_project for first 24h after signup. low-cost guardrail.
Priya Patel: customer replied: "Thanks — confirmed 200s now. please rotate the key for us and we'll confirm in our staging. appreciate the fast help :thumbsup:"
Ingrid M: scheduled rotation for 1767123500 and will close once customer verifies.
Priya Patel: closing thread once rotation verified. thanks team :raised_hands:
